The accused in C.C. No. 291 of 2005 on the files of the Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Manjeri, filed this Revision Petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16 (IA) (i), 2(ia) and 7(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short "the PFA Act") read with Rule 29 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955(for short "the PFA Rules").
2. Heard.
3.

sentences.text:
The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
Crl.Revision Petition No. 812 of 2013 On 22-08-2005 at about 1.30 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 900 gram of fried green peas from the first accused.
The 2nd accused was the licensee of the shop.
After sampling as per Rules, one sample was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis.

The Public Analyst, after analysis,
submitted Ext. P11 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for the food item under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 and was therefore, adulterated.
Thereafter, on the request of the accused, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis.
Ext.P21 certificate of the Central Food Laboratory would show that the sample contained living insects and hence it was unfit for human consumption and therefore, the same was adulterated.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts. P1 to P21 were marked for the prosecution.
No evidence was adduced on the side of the Crl.Revision Petition No. 812 of 2013 revision petitioners.

5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P21 cannot be acted upon to hold that P.T.Asharaf vs The State Of Kerala on 14 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125718810/

The learned counsel for the revision petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A)
(ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act.

Therefore, Ext. P21 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased Crl.Revision Petition No. 812 of 2013 in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra).

It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal.

In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the revision petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor.

Even otherwise, in view of the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra), the conviction in this case cannot be sustained as no laboratory was notified and no validated Crl.Revision Petition No. 812 of 2013 method of analysis was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
In the result, this Revision Petition stands allowed, setting aside the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under 16 (IA) (i), 2(ia) and 7(i) of the PFA Act read with Rule 29 of PFA Rules and the revision petitioners are acquitted for the said offence.
The bail bonds of the revision petitioners stand cancelled and they are set at liberty.
SD/- B. SUDHEENDRA KUMAR, JUDGE.
